tip: Russian good wishes use the genitive: Хорошего полёта (Khoroshego polyota = of a good flight), literally wishing you 'of a good flight'.
нужна (nuzhna = needed) agrees with the thing needed, not the person: помощь (pomoshch = help) is feminine, so нужна, not нужен.
к (k) means toward and takes the dative: к остановке (k ostanovke = up to the stop). Use it for approaching a point.
With понравился (ponravilsya = was liked), the liker goes dative, Друзьям (Druzyam = to friends), and the verb agrees with the thing liked, дом (dom = house).
вкусно готовят (vkusno gotovyat) has no subject, meaning 'people cook deliciously'; subjectless 'they' becomes an English passive: the food is delicious.
идём (idyom = we go) is for going on foot; ехать (yekhat = go by vehicle) is for vehicles. Russian marks how you travel, English uses 'go' for both.
несколько (neskolko = several) takes the genitive plural: несколько студентов (studentov = of students). Quantity words govern the genitive.
по-русски (po-russki = in Russian) is how you name a language of speech: по- plus the adverb, hyphenated and lowercase, never capitalized.
нельзя (nelzya = not allowed) puts the person in the dative: Детям нельзя (Detyam nelzya = children may not). There is no verb 'to be'.
A few masculine nouns take a stressed -у in the locative: в саду (v sadu = in the garden), not в саде (v sade). Same for в лесу (v lesu), на мосту (na mostu).
For games, use играть в (igrat v = play) plus the accusative: играет в шахматы (igrayet v shakhmaty = plays chess). Instruments take играть на (igrat na).
с (s) means 'with' and takes the instrumental: с вами (s vami = with you). The verb познакомиться (poznakomitsya = get acquainted) always pairs with с.
Russian counts toward the coming hour: Половина пятого (Polovina pyatogo = half of the fifth) is 4:30, halfway to five. пятого is genitive.
